sources.entry: vir by Djordje Marković - Distills the Claude Code transcripts already on your disk into typed markdown notes (decisions, gotchas, patterns). Serves them via MCP and a CLAUDE.md block. Integrates with Obsidian.

summary.one_liner: vir is a Node/TypeScript CLI that distills your Claude Code and Codex session transcripts into typed, plain-markdown notes (patterns, gotchas, decisions, tools) that work in an Obsidian vault or any folder.
summary.what_it_does: vir reads transcripts from ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions, filters out subagent, workflow and headless SDK runs, classifies the remaining sessions with a cheap model (Haiku in the README's defaults), and distills durable knowledge with a stronger model (Sonnet by default). Output is markdown with YAML frontmatter and confidence scores, written into a folder that can be an Obsidian vault or any directory. Other inputs include clipped web articles and PDFs. Retrieval is via `vir query` (TF-IDF by default, or optional embeddings through Ollama or a local fastembed model), and an MCP server exposes six tools to Claude Code or Codex mid-session. `vir sync-claude` can inject top notes into CLAUDE.md and existing AGENTS.md files after a diff and confirmation, and `vir review`, `vir lint`, `vir dedupe` and `vir audit` support curation. A daemon can be scheduled via launchd or systemd/cron.
use_cases: Recover decisions and gotchas from old Claude Code sessions before they are pruned
Build a searchable personal knowledge base from coding agent history
Give Claude Code or Codex access to past project lessons via MCP
Keep CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md updated with reviewed lessons
Browse AI-session-derived notes in an Obsidian vault
Synthesize topic pages from related notes
notable: Retroactive distillation: turns months of existing Claude Code and Codex transcripts into notes in one run, before Claude Code prunes them
Works without Obsidian: output is plain markdown and vir query and the MCP server run with no editor
Quality controls: project include/exclude triage, confidence scores, human review with verified-note boost, and rules from `vir connect` that need explicit approval
Zero-dollar options via claude-cli or codex-cli providers, which consume subscription quota and cap runs at 25 sessions
Reversible actions: rejected and pruned notes move to .rejected/ rather than being deleted
caveats: Platform support: macOS is stable; Linux (systemd and cron) is marked experimental and untested; Windows is not supported
Cursor sessions are not supported yet (planned); the README lists Codex as new in 0.26
codex-cli provider is marked experimental; claude-cli and codex-cli distills consume subscription usage limits
Costs apply for API providers; README cites ~$1 to $5 first-run cost and ~$0.05 per run ongoing, and Kie.ai is noted as not recommended for a real vault
